title: NC / share-alike vs CC-BY acceptance policy
context: Candidate teaching datasets carry non-commercial (NC) and share-alike clauses that must be reconciled with the project's CC-BY-4.0 content license and MIT code license. This task defines, explicitly, when NC and share-alike sources are acceptable and how conflicts with the CC-BY content license are flagged.
objective: Specify the acceptance policy for NC and share-alike licensed sources versus the project's CC-BY-4.0 content license, with a clear decision rule the dataset gate and reviewers apply.
acceptanceCriteria: States when NC sources are acceptable (non-commercial educational use, honoured and clearly labelled in lesson and any republished derivative).
States when share-alike sources are acceptable (only if we can comply) and how any conflict with the CC-BY content license is flagged.
Defines the fallback for closed/ambiguous/'academic-only/no-redistribution' sources: fetch-by-script never vendored, or exclude.
Aligns with the gate-001 pass/exclude rule; reviewed by License+Data-Ethics.
resources: PLAN.md (binding cancer guardrails / Data, licensing & compliance)
